scenes.audio: Marcus signs an application and pays an initial premium. Has he automatically received every benefit he requested?
scenes.label: Opening Hook
scenes.visual: Static wide shot on a matte beige background. A white rectangular card slides in from the left, followed by a green arrow and a dark gray card. Flat, even lighting with no shadows.

scenes.audio: Not necessarily. A valid contract needs agreement, consideration, competent parties, and a legal purpose.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Continuation of the previous layout. A third card in light blue appears to the right of the dark gray card. The color palette is muted and professional.

scenes.audio: The application commonly constitutes an offer and the insurer decides whether to accept under its rules.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Static frame showing three info cards connected by arrows. The graphic remains centered. Lighting is consistent and artificial.

scenes.audio: If it offers different coverage or a higher premium, that may be a counteroffer requiring acceptance.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Graphics remain static on the beige background. The focus is on the textual flow between the three boxes.

scenes.audio: The precise effective date also depends on the application, receipt, and policy conditions.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Static view of the insurance contract flow diagram. High contrast between text and card backgrounds.

scenes.audio: A signature or payment alone is not a universal coverage rule.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Final static view of the 'from application to agreement' flow. The circular gold logo is visible in the bottom left corner.

scenes.audio: Consideration is the value exchanged for the contractual promise.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: Scene transition to a new layout. Three vertical cards (white, green, and cream) appear side-by-side. The header changes to a different topic.

scenes.audio: The applicant supplies the premium and application statements.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: Static layout of the three vertical cards. Earthy color tones are dominant. Lighting remains flat and digital.

scenes.audio: The insurer supplies its promise to pay according to the contract. Competent parties must have the legal capacity to contract.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: Vertical cards remain fixed in the frame. Subject focus is on the central and rightmost boxes.

scenes.audio: A lawful purpose means the arrangement cannot be built around an illegal objective.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: The screen remains static with the three vertical boxes. The gold circular emblem sits at the bottom left.

scenes.audio: Life insurance on another person also raises insurable interest and consent requirements.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: Graphics remain static. The composition is clean with ample negative space around the boxes.

scenes.audio: Insurance is commonly described as a contract of adhesion because the insurer prepares the standard terms
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: Layout shifts to two side-by-side cards: one white and one dark teal. Beige background continues.

scenes.audio: and the applicant generally accepts or rejects them. That does not mean a clear exclusion disappears.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: Static shot of the two-box layout. Text descriptions are visible within the cards.

scenes.audio: We will study interpretation separately. The contract is also aleatory. The value exchanged depends on an uncertain event and may be unequal.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: Static view of the 'Adhesion' and 'Aleatory' cards. Minimalist design with sharp corners on UI elements.

scenes.audio: Marcus could pay a relatively small amount before a covered death produces a large benefit. Another insured may pay premiums for many years.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: The graphic layout remains unchanged. Lighting is uniform across the beige field.

scenes.audio: A life policy is usually described as unilateral because the insurer makes the enforceable promise to pay covered benefits.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: New graphic layout: two boxes labeled with different legal characteristics. White and teal color scheme.

scenes.audio: The owner can generally stop paying future premiums, subject to policy consequences such as lapse or use of available values.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: Static shot of the 'Unilateral' and 'Conditional' boxes. Text details are brief and centered.

scenes.audio: This does not mean the policy has no conditions. Coverage may depend on required premiums, truthful application information, and other valid terms.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: Continuation of the static dual-box layout. Professional academic presentation style.

scenes.audio: Indemnity generally aims to compensate an actual covered financial loss without creating a profit from that loss.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: Three vertical boxes appear: white, light green, and light blue. The beige background is consistent.

scenes.audio: Life insurance ordinarily pays a stated contractual death benefit rather than measuring the person's economic worth after death.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: Static shot of the three vertical cards. Graphics are sharp with high contrast.

scenes.audio: The personal contract concept also needs care. Many insurance contracts closely connect coverage to a particular insured risk.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: Static layout remains on screen. Bottom logo is gold and black.

scenes.audio: But life policies generally permit assignment of ownership rights. Assignment does not change which person's life is insured.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: Graphics remain static. The boxes provide definitions for legal terms.

scenes.audio: Suppose an applicant requests one rate, but the insurer offers a higher rate based on underwriting.
scenes.label: Call to Action
scenes.visual: The screen clears and a numbered list of four items appears sequentially. Header reads 'Read the facts in order'.

scenes.audio: Identify the counteroffer and the applicant's response before assuming a contract on the original terms.
scenes.label: Call to Action
scenes.visual: Static list of four items on a beige background. Professional typography.

scenes.audio: Then check the consideration, legal capacity, and lawful purpose.
scenes.label: Call to Action
scenes.visual: The numbered list remains on screen. Uniform lighting across the digital canvas.

scenes.audio: Finally, apply the policy's conditions. The exam may ask only for a characteristic, such as aleatory or adhesion.
scenes.label: Call to Action
scenes.visual: Static shot of the final list. Muted earth tones on the UI elements.

scenes.audio: But a real file can involve several at once. Learn the reason each term fits so a changed scenario does not depend on memorized wording.
scenes.label: Call to Action
scenes.visual: Static list remains until the video ends. Minimalistic layout focuses on readability.
